content.user_title: Manage Fabric Capacities with Azure .NET SDK
content.value_statement: Fabric capacity administration requires correct Azure SDK patterns and careful authentication. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused .NET guidance for ARM-based capacity tasks.
actual_capabilities: Shows package installation for Azure.ResourceManager.Fabric and Azure.Identity.
Explains DefaultAzureCredential setup for Fabric capacity management.
Provides .NET examples for create, read, update, suspend, resume, and delete operations.
Lists Fabric capacity SKUs, resource states, and provisioning states.
Documents name availability checks and available SKU discovery.
Includes Azure RequestFailedException handling patterns for ARM operations.
limitations: Covers the Azure management plane, not Fabric workspace or data plane APIs.
Requires valid Azure credentials, subscription access, and Fabric permissions.
Examples must be adapted to the target resource group, region, and governance policy.
Does not replace testing, quota checks, or cloud change approval processes.

use_cases.title: Provision Fabric Capacity
use_cases.description: Create a .NET workflow that provisions a Fabric capacity with location, SKU, tags, and administrators.

use_cases.title: Maintain Capacity Settings
use_cases.description: Update administrators, scale SKUs, and check resource states during operational changes.

use_cases.title: Build ARM Automation
use_cases.description: Add Fabric capacity checks, error handling, and SKU discovery to internal cloud tooling.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the SDK Scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain what Azure.ResourceManager.Fabric can manage in .NET, and list what it cannot manage.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Capacity Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a Fabric capacity in .NET using DefaultAzureCredential, resource group access, SKU selection, and administrator assignment.

prompt_templates.title: Add Operational Checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a .NET flow that checks Fabric capacity name availability, lists available SKUs, and handles common ARM errors.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Fabric capacity automation plan for authentication, permissions, long-running operations, error handling, and safe scale or delete controls.

output_examples.input: Explain how to create a Fabric capacity with the Azure .NET SDK.
output_examples.output: A concise implementation plan covering required packages, Azure authentication, resource group lookup, capacity data, SKU choice, and operation completion.

output_examples.input: Help me troubleshoot a failed capacity creation request.
output_examples.output: A diagnostic checklist for ARM status codes, invalid configuration, quota limits, region availability, permissions, and administrator identity issues.

output_examples.input: Compare management plane and data plane Fabric SDK usage.
output_examples.output: A clear distinction between capacity administration through Azure Resource Manager and workspace item operations through Fabric data plane APIs.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential and avoid hardcoded Azure secrets.
Check SKU availability, location support, and quotas before provisioning.
Require explicit approval before scale, suspend, resume, or delete actions.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for Fabric workspace, lakehouse, warehouse, or item operations.
Do not run capacity changes without validating subscription, resource group, and region.
Do not expose tenant IDs, client IDs, client secrets, or administrator identities in logs.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps users work with the Azure Resource Manager Fabric SDK for .NET capacity management.

faq.question: Can it manage Fabric workspaces or lakehouses?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on capacity resources. Use Fabric data plane APIs for workspace and item operations.

faq.question: Does it require Azure credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples assume Azure authentication through DefaultAzureCredential and appropriate subscription permissions.

faq.question: Can it help with scaling a capacity?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows update patterns for SKU changes and notes that scaling can take time.

faq.question: Does it include destructive operations?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents suspend, resume, and delete examples. Users should require approval before those actions.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
